block.title: Typed SerenityOS syscalls check their memory in libpizlo
block.p: A spike tested how a pizlonated SerenityOS LibC could make system calls. Serenity's LibSystem casts every argument to an integer, which drops each pointer's capability. Under Fil-C, the spike turns syscall(SC_foo, ...) into a call of a typed libpizlo native. It generates the types from the kernel's own sys$foo declarations and describes each parameter struct once, field by field.

claim.p: The rewritten Syscall.h keeps the layout of all 49 parameter structs, and Serenity's LibC compiles against it unchanged. A libpizlo built with seven of the natives stops a lying string length, a freed string, oversized buffers, a forged pointer and an oversized addrlen, each with a safety error inside the native.

block.p: The typed path also found that Serenity's setregid() calls SC_setresgid with two arguments instead of three, so the kernel reads a garbage saved gid. Keeping Fil-C's pizlonated glibc on top would not work: libpizlo passes Linux flags and structs straight through, and Serenity's differ.
